\section[\ml{വസന്തകാലം} \ml{വേനൽക്കാലം} \ml{മഴക്കാലം} \ml{ശൈത്യകാലം}]{\ml{വസന്തകാലം}, \ml{വേനൽ}, \ml{മഴ}, \ml{ശൈത്യം} — the same pattern as Tamil}

\label{lesson:ML-C14-kaalangal}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} Malayalam's season words follow the very same recipe as Tamil's — native words for what a season \emph{feels like}, plus one shared Sanskrit loan for spring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know}
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Malayalam} & \textbf{meaning} & \textbf{source} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{വസന്തകാലം}} (\emph{vasanthakaalam}) & \textquotedblleft{}spring\textquotedblright{} & \emph{vasantham} — the same \textbf{Sanskrit} loan as Tamil \\
\textbf{\ml{വേനൽക്കാലം}} (\emph{venalkkaalam}) & \textquotedblleft{}summer\textquotedblright{} & \textbf{\ml{വേനൽ}} \emph{venal}, native Dravidian, matching Tamil \emph{kodai}'s role \\
\textbf{\ml{മഴക്കാലം}} (\emph{mazhakkaalam}) & \textquotedblleft{}rainy season\textquotedblright{} & \textbf{\ml{മഴ}} \emph{mazha}, native Dravidian, matching Tamil \emph{mazhai} closely \\
\textbf{\ml{ശൈത്യകാലം}} (\emph{śaithyakaalam}) & \textquotedblleft{}winter/cold season\textquotedblright{} & \emph{śaithya} — this one leans more \textbf{Sanskrit-flavored} than Tamil's native \emph{kulir} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Every one shares the ending \textbf{‑\ml{കാലം}} (\emph{‑kaalam}, \textquotedblleft{}time/season\textquotedblright{}) — itself ultimately from Sanskrit \textbf{\dv{काल}} (\emph{kāla}), but assimilated so long ago that it functions as ordinary vocabulary, quite unlike a fresher loan like \emph{vasantham}.

\begin{culture}
As with Tamil, Kerala's actual climate is shaped far more by \textbf{\ml{മഴക്കാലം}} (\emph{mazhakkaalam}, \textquotedblleft{}the rains\textquotedblright{} — including Kerala's famous southwest monsoon) than by a clean four-way Western split. The rains aren't a footnote to \textquotedblleft{}summer\textquotedblright{} or \textquotedblleft{}autumn\textquotedblright{} — they're their own major season, central to daily and agricultural life.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Guided Practice}
{[}PAUSE 1s{]}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item {[}YOU SAY: \textquotedblleft{}venal\textquotedblright{} — summer heat — then \textquotedblleft{}kaalam,\textquotedblright{} season{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: \textquotedblleft{}mazhakkaalam\textquotedblright{} — the rains, the real central season{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: \textquotedblleft{}śaithyakaalam\textquotedblright{} — the cold season{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: the shared loanword — \textquotedblleft{}vasanthakaalam,\textquotedblright{} spring, same as Tamil{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Wrap-up recall}]
{[}PAUSE 3s{]} Which Malayalam season-words match Tamil's closely, and which is shared with Tamil as a Sanskrit loan? (\textbf{Venal/mazha} match Tamil's \emph{kodai/mazhai}; \textbf{vasanthakaalam} is the same Sanskrit loan as Tamil's \emph{vasantha kaalam}.) What's the real central season in Kerala's climate? (\textbf{Mazhakkaalam}, the rains/monsoon.)
\end{tcolorbox}
